scope: Proposition 10.5 (Three-quarter list entropy) of the manuscript “Conditional information under deterministic coordinate sweeps” (preprints/Conditional-information-under-deterministic-coordinate-sweeps-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 238 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ad4125b0a60530a3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 47. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every integer b ≥ 1, every deterministic starting deck, and any ordered list of k ≤ 3n/4 distinct labels, the endpoint law µb,k after b sweeps satisfies, for sufficiently large d, D(µb,k∥Uinj,k) ≤ n2 n−(b−1)/64 . (10.9) In particular at b = 769, every such list has total-variation error at most n−5.
